question: Which cellular layer forms the main wall of a tiny blood capillary?
explanation: Capillaries consist of a single layer of flat, squamous endothelial cells which makes their walls extremely thin for substance exchange. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h1)

question: Why do red blood cells often travel through narrow capillaries in single file?

options.A: To prevent the vessel walls from collapsing under pressure
options.B: To speed up the total flow rate of blood through the organ
options.C: To maximize their exposure to surrounding tissue walls
options.D: To allow white blood cells to squeeze past them easily

explanation: Narrow capillary width forces red blood cells into single file, bringing almost every cell close to the wall for efficient gas exchange. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h1)

question: Which type of capillary features tiny pores or windows in its walls for rapid fluid filtration?
explanation: Fenestrated capillaries have small pores that allow rapid exchange of fluids and small solutes, common in filtering organs like kidneys. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h2)

question: Where are sinusoidal capillaries with large gaps typically found in the body?
explanation: Sinusoidal capillaries have very large gaps that allow whole blood cells to pass through, which is necessary in blood-forming and filtering organs like the liver and spleen. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h2)

question: What structures directly control the entry of blood into true capillary networks?
explanation: Precapillary sphincters are rings of smooth muscle that open and close to direct blood flow into the capillary beds as needed. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h3)

question: What happens to precapillary sphincters when a tissue has a high demand for oxygen?

options.A: They relax to let more blood flow through the capillaries
options.B: They multiply in number to increase the surface area
options.C: They contract tightly to shunt blood past the tissue
options.D: They swell up and block the metarteriole completely

explanation: When tissues are active and need oxygen, local chemical changes cause precapillary sphincters to relax, opening the beds for maximum nutrient delivery. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary way that oxygen and carbon dioxide cross capillary walls?
explanation: Gases move freely down their concentration gradients across the capillary membrane via simple diffusion. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h4)

question: Which force primarily drives fluid out of a capillary and into the surrounding tissues?
explanation: Capillary hydrostatic pressure pushes fluids and dissolved small molecules out of the vessel through filtration. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h4)

question: What happens to fluid movement at the start end of a capillary bed?

options.A: Lymphatic vessels push fluid into the capillary
options.B: Net filtration pushes fluid out into the tissues
options.D: Net absorption pulls fluid back into the blood

explanation: Higher hydrostatic pressure at the arteriolar end causes fluid to filter out into the interstitial space. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h5)

question: Why does fluid return to the capillary near the venular end?

options.A: Tissue hydrostatic pressure rises higher than the blood pressure
options.B: Red blood cells actively pump water back through the vessel walls
options.C: The lymphatic system forces fluid backward into the veins
options.D: Capillary blood pressure drops while plasma colloid osmotic pressure remains steady

explanation: As blood travels through the capillary, hydrostatic pressure falls below the osmotic pull of plasma proteins, drawing fluid back in. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the abnormal buildup of fluid in tissue spaces?
explanation: Edema is swelling caused by excess fluid building up in the tissues when capillary filtration outpaces absorption and drainage. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h6)

question: A pregnant woman develops lower leg swelling due to increased venous pressure in the pelvis. Which factor has primarily changed?

options.B: Interstitial fluid pressure dropped to zero

explanation: Raised venous pressure backs up blood into the capillaries, increasing hydrostatic pressure and forcing excess fluid out into the tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h6)
